title: The Protocol of Marseille's old port
premise: Dominic Thornbury, a disgraced air-crash investigator haunted by the deaths of her family in row twelve of Flight 4471, is summoned to Marseille when every record of a passenger flight vanishes from radar, databases, and memory while the plane is still airborne. Teaming with a rogue air traffic controller, Elias Marchetti, and an Interpol analyst hiding her own loyalties, she uncovers a conspiracy to stage a mid-air catastrophe as an 'accident' to bury a witness to a state-level arms deal. As Dominic races to decode the protocol behind the erasure, she must choose between the duty that once consumed her and the fragile found family forming around her. In the climax over the Mediterranean, she forces the aircraft down at Marseille's old port, exposing the plotters, and finally allows herself to grieve—and belong.
about_author: Jude Reyes is a former maritime journalist who spent a decade covering port cities from Genoa to Piraeus before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people rebuilding themselves in the shadows of institutions, and lives between Marseille and Lisbon.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Opening in a Marseille archive, Dominic catalogues wreckage from a minor crash no airline wants attributed, flashing back to the night she lost her family. Emotional beat: grief calcified into routine, and the first tremor that her careful detachment is cracking.

chapters.title: The Flight That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A colleague calls at 3 a.m.: Flight AX-217 is still in the air, yet its flight plan, passenger manifest, and maintenance logs have been wiped from every system. Dominic verifies it herself. Beat: cold dread replacing professional calm as the impossible becomes real.

chapters.title: Controller Down
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Air traffic controller Elias Marchetti, the last person to speak with AX-217, is suspended and silenced by his own agency. He goes off-grid, carrying a recorded transmission no one else has heard. Beat: paranoia and the stubborn instinct to protect the truth.

chapters.title: Attribution Denied
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Official channels refuse to acknowledge AX-217 existed; her access is revoked and she's branded unstable. She realizes whoever erased the flight can erase people too. Beat: isolation sharpening into defiance as she decides to investigate off the books.

chapters.title: Two Strangers, One Frequency
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Dominic tracks Elias through the recording he leaked to a pirate radio hobbyist. Their first meeting in a Vieux-Port bar is hostile, wary, mutually useful. Beat: the awkward first stitch of trust between two people trained to trust no one.

chapters.title: The Witness in 14C
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Digging into the vanished manifest, Dominic identifies passenger Nadia Osei, an arms-deal accountant scheduled to testify in The Hague. AX-217 was never the target—Nadia was. Beat: the case turns personal; the accident was always going to be manufactured.

chapters.title: Interpol's Quiet Room
chapters.summary: Camille's POV. Introduce Interpol analyst Camille Duras, assigned to discredit Dominic. Camille recognizes the erasure signature—she's seen it before and buried it. Beat: complicity and conscience at war; she begins feeding Dominic fragments anonymously.

chapters.title: Protocol Zero
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias and Dominic decode the transmission: 'Protocol Zero,' a cyber-weapon that rewrites flight data in real time, built to make any aircraft disappear from the record mid-flight. Beat: awe and horror—the scale of the machinery against three unarmed people.

chapters.title: The Arms Dealer's Harbor
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Following Nadia's financial trail to Marseille's port warehouses, Dominic finds the deal's broker, Aurel Voss, and barely escapes his cleaners. Beat: fear made physical; the enemy has a face and it is patient.

chapters.title: Camille Crosses
chapters.summary: Camille's POV. Camille's anonymous warnings are traced; cornered, she defects outright, bringing Interpol files that name Voss's state patrons. Beat: the cost of conscience, and the found family gaining a third, reluctant member.

chapters.title: What the Sea Keeps
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. A quiet interlude: the three hide on Elias's boat. Dominic finally tells the story of row twelve—how she identified her own family's bodies. Beat: grief shared for the first time; love beginning where duty once lived.

chapters.title: A Second Flight
chapters.summary: Camille's POV. Camille discovers Protocol Zero will run again—on a charter from Marseille carrying Nadia Osei, extracted from protective custody by Voss's people. Beat: the trap closes; the attack is scheduled to look like an accident, just like before.

chapters.title: Manifest of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic infiltrates the handling agent's office to confirm the charter's tail number and finds her own name added to a doctored accident report—she is meant to die aboard. Beat: the enemy knows her; terror fusing into resolve.

chapters.title: Twelve Hours
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The team splits: Camille works diplomatic channels, Elias preps the control tower he's barred from, Dominic goes after the Protocol Zero operator. Beat: ticking-clock tension; every plan has a hole and they know it.

chapters.title: The Operator
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic traces the weapon's operator to a data center above the old port and confronts him—a hollow man who erased his own daughter's crash to stop an investigation. Beat: a dark mirror of her grief; mercy offered, refused.

chapters.title: Wheels Up
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The charter departs with Nadia aboard and Protocol Zero armed; Elias talks his way into the tower as the aircraft blinks out of every screen. Beat: helplessness at altitude—the attack has begun and they are the only ones who can see it.

chapters.title: Vanishing Point
chapters.summary: Camille's POV. Camille broadcasts the evidence to allied agencies as Voss's patrons try to scrub her too; she goes public, burning her career to keep the story alive. Beat: sacrifice—truth as a relay baton passed hand to hand.

chapters.title: Talk Her Down
chapters.summary: Dominic and Elias's POV. Dominic reaches the cockpit via the operator's backdoor; the pilots, flying blind in erased airspace, trust a voice they cannot verify. Beat: raw human connection across a radio—the whole conspiracy reduced to one voice choosing to be believed.

chapters.title: The Old Port
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias guides the crippled charter to an emergency descent over Vieux-Port as Voss's second team tries to force a crash; Dominic confronts Voss on the quay. Beat: climax—Voss falls, the plane lands hard but intact, and the port holds its breath.

chapters.title: Attribution
chapters.summary: Camille's POV. In the aftermath, the evidence lands; Voss's patrons fall in three capitals, and the world finally attributes AX-217 correctly. Nadia testifies. Beat: vindication that tastes like ash—truth won, but slowly, and at cost.

chapters.title: Empty Chairs
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic visits the memorial wall, adds no new names for once, and lets herself weep for row twelve without shame. Beat: grief transmuted—the investigator who lived in wreckage learns to live beside the living.

chapters.title: The Protocol of Belonging
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, closing. Weeks later, Dominic, Elias, and Camille share a slow breakfast above the old port; a new case file waits, and for the first time she won't open it alone. Beat: found family as the true protocol—love, finally, against and beyond duty.
